## Recent Research on Structured Pruning and Reasoning LLMs

### Key Finding on Structured Pruning's Limitations

Structured pruning methods that remove entire sets of layer blocks have been shown to significantly degrade test-time scaling reasoning performance in reasoning LLMs. However, recent experiments across four reasoning benchmarks on two reasoning LLMs (s1.1-7B and Qwen3-8B) consistently show that unstructured pruning can augment test-time scaling performance compared to structured pruning, and at times can even outperform unpruned full-weight LLMs.

### Recent Advances in Structured Pruning

**GPrune-LLM (March 2026):** GPrune-LLM is a generalization-aware structured pruning framework that accounts for neuron differences in cross-distribution behavior and addresses the fact that most existing methods estimate neuron importance from activation statistics on a single calibration dataset, which introduces calibration bias and degrades downstream cross-task generalization.

**DieT (Dimension-wise Pruning):** DieT achieves comprehensive zero-shot results across two model scales, seven benchmarks, and sparsity up to 20% showing consistent gains over state-of-the-art pruning baselines.

### Key Takeaway

The 2026 research landscape suggests that while structured pruning is useful for general compression, carefully undertaken pruning can improve test-time scaling effectiveness even further, though unstructured approaches may be preferable for reasoning-specific tasks.

  # === Direct Competitors ===
  - id: self_healing_2025
    title: "Self-Healing: Recovering Pruned Large Reasoning Models via Reinforcement Learning"
    year: 2025
    venue: "under review"
    category: direct-competitor
    role: "RLVR recovery baseline"
    relevance: 9
    key_finding: "RLVR recovers 95%+ at 25% compression; SFT only reaches ~80%"
    our_relation: "We extend beyond single sparsity ratio and add CKA-guided pruning selection"
    arxiv_id: ""

  - id: resp_2025
    title: "RESP: Self-Reflective Structured Pruning for Reasoning LLMs"
    year: 2025
    venue: "arXiv Dec 2025"
    category: direct-competitor
    role: "Structured pruning for reasoning without recovery"
    relevance: 8
    key_finding: "GSM8K 81.3% at 40% sparsity via self-reflective importance"
    our_relation: "No RLVR recovery; we show recovery-aware pruning outperforms at same sparsity"
    arxiv_id: ""

  - id: grasprune_2026
    title: "GRASPrune: Global Gating-based Structural Pruning for LLMs"
    year: 2026
    venue: "ACL 2026 Main"
    category: direct-competitor
    role: "SOTA budgeted structural pruning"
    relevance: 8
    key_finding: "Global gating achieves best structured pruning under budget constraints"
    our_relation: "GRASPrune as pruning backbone; we add CKA overlap + RLVR recovery on top"
    arxiv_id: ""

  - id: opsd_2026
    title: "OPSD: One-shot Post-RL Structured Distillation"
    year: 2026
    venue: "arXiv May 2026"
    category: direct-competitor
    role: "Post-RL compression via distillation"
    relevance: 7
    key_finding: "Compress post-RL model in one shot via structured distillation"
    our_relation: "Distillation-based vs our pruning+recovery approach; complementary"
    arxiv_id: ""

  - id: doing_more_with_less_2026
    title: "Doing More With Less: Revisiting the Effectiveness of LLM Pruning for Test-Time Scaling"
    year: 2026
    venue: "arXiv Apr 2026"
    category: direct-competitor
    role: "Pruning improves test-time scaling"
    relevance: 7
    key_finding: "Unstructured pruning can augment test-time scaling; structured pruning degrades it"
    our_relation: "Motivates why structured pruning needs recovery; we address this gap with RLVR"
    arxiv_id: "2604.25098"

  - id: gprune_llm_2026
    title: "GPrune-LLM: Generalization-Aware Structured Pruning for Large Language Models"
    year: 2026
    venue: "arXiv Mar 2026"
    category: direct-competitor
    role: "Cross-distribution generalization-aware pruning"
    relevance: 6
    key_finding: "Accounts for neuron cross-distribution behavior; reduces calibration bias"
    our_relation: "Complementary importance metric; our CKA captures functional overlap vs their generalization gap"
    arxiv_id: "2603.13418"

  # === Method Components ===
  - id: mpruner_2024
    title: "MPruner: CKA-based Inter-layer Pruning for LLMs"
    year: 2024
    venue: "arXiv"
    category: method-component
    role: "CKA for layer importance estimation"
    relevance: 8
    key_finding: "CKA similarity between layers identifies redundant layers for removal"
    our_relation: "We adapt CKA from layer-level to width-level functional overlap prediction"
    arxiv_id: ""

  - id: lachance_thesis_2024
    title: "CKA Layer Similarity for Neural Network Pruning"
    year: 2024
    venue: "URI Master's Thesis"
    category: method-component
    role: "CKA-based pruning theoretical foundation"
    relevance: 6
    key_finding: "CKA layer similarity correlates with pruning recoverability"
    our_relation: "Validates CKA as signal for pruning decisions; we extend to predict RLVR recovery"
    arxiv_id: ""

  - id: bonsai_2025
    title: "Bonsai: Gradient-Free Structured Pruning for LLMs"
    year: 2025
    venue: "ICML 2025"
    category: method-component
    role: "Gradient-free structured pruning alternative"
    relevance: 6
    key_finding: "Achieves competitive structured pruning without backprop"
    our_relation: "Alternative pruning strategy; our CKA metric is also gradient-free"
    arxiv_id: ""

  - id: pat_2025
    title: "PAT: Pruning-Aware Tuning for LLMs"
    year: 2025
    venue: "AAAI 2025"
    category: method-component
    role: "Joint pruning and tuning framework"
    relevance: 6
    key_finding: "Co-optimizing pruning mask and fine-tuning improves recovery"
    our_relation: "Related idea of pruning-tuning interaction; we separate pruning and RLVR recovery"
    arxiv_id: ""

  - id: rac_2025
    title: "RAC: Chain-of-Thought Reconstruction for Pruned Reasoning Models"
    year: 2025
    venue: "NeurIPS 2025"
    category: method-component
    role: "CoT reconstruction post-pruning"
    relevance: 7
    key_finding: "Reconstructing CoT improves unstructured/2:4 pruned reasoning models"
    our_relation: "Complementary recovery strategy; could combine with our RLVR approach"
    arxiv_id: ""

  - id: paser_2025
    title: "PASER: Data Selection for Pruning Recovery"
    year: 2025
    venue: "under review"
    category: method-component
    role: "Recovery training data selection"
    relevance: 6
    key_finding: "Selective data for recovery training improves efficiency"
    our_relation: "Orthogonal contribution; can apply PASER data selection to our RLVR recovery"
    arxiv_id: ""

  # === Background / Theory ===
  - id: rl_squeezes_2026
    title: "RL Squeezes, SFT Expands: Different Mechanisms in Post-Training"
    year: 2026
    venue: "ICLR 2026 Poster"
    category: background
    role: "Theoretical basis for why RLVR works differently from SFT"
    relevance: 8
    key_finding: "RLVR compresses representation while SFT expands; different inductive biases"
    our_relation: "Explains why RLVR recovery succeeds where SFT fails post-pruning"
    arxiv_id: ""

  - id: from_llms_to_lrms_2026
    title: "From LLMs to LRMs: Width Pruning is More Robust for Reasoning"
    year: 2026
    venue: "arXiv Jan 2026"
    category: background
    role: "Width vs depth pruning for reasoning"
    relevance: 7
    key_finding: "Width pruning preserves reasoning better than depth pruning"
    our_relation: "Motivates our focus on width-level structured pruning"
    arxiv_id: ""

  - id: p2_law_2025
    title: "P² Law: Scaling Law for Pruning Recovery Training"
    year: 2025
    venue: "ACL 2025"
    category: background
    role: "Theoretical scaling of recovery compute"
    relevance: 7
    key_finding: "Recovery training follows predictable scaling with compute and data"
    our_relation: "Informs our recovery budget estimation; we extend to RLVR-specific scaling"
    arxiv_id: ""

  - id: mipp_2024
    title: "MIPP: Mutual Information Preserving Pruning"
    year: 2024
    venue: "arXiv"
    category: background
    role: "Information-theoretic pruning criterion"
    relevance: 5
    key_finding: "Preserving mutual information between layers reduces pruning damage"
    our_relation: "Related theoretical motivation; CKA captures similar functional redundancy"
    arxiv_id: ""

  - id: redundancy_aware_cnn_2020
    title: "Redundancy-Aware Pruning of Convolutional Neural Networks"
    year: 2020
    venue: "Neural Computation"
    category: background
    role: "Pioneer of redundancy-based pruning"
    relevance: 4
    key_finding: "Redundancy metrics guide pruning decisions in CNNs"
    our_relation: "Conceptual ancestor; we apply redundancy-awareness to LLM structured pruning"
    arxiv_id: ""

  - id: self_distilled_rlvr_2026
    title: "Self-Distilled RLVR"
    year: 2026
    venue: "arXiv Apr 2026"
    category: background
    role: "RLVR training efficiency improvement"
    relevance: 5
    key_finding: "Self-distillation stabilizes RLVR training and improves sample efficiency"
    our_relation: "Could improve our RLVR recovery phase efficiency"
    arxiv_id: "2604.03128"

  - id: diet_2026
    title: "DieT: Dimension-wise Global Pruning via Task-specific Importance Score"
    year: 2026
    venue: "arXiv Mar 2026"
    category: background
    role: "Dimension-wise importance for width pruning"
    relevance: 5
    key_finding: "Task-specific dimension importance outperforms activation-based metrics at 20-40% sparsity"
    our_relation: "Alternative width importance metric; we use CKA overlap instead"
    arxiv_id: "2603.23985"
